title: Intelligent rate smoothing and autoscaler heuristics for vector service
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Goal: Improve end-to-end embedding throughput and p99 latency stability during bursty tenant traffic by combining rate-smoothing at the router layer with a predictive autoscaler for vector workers. Background: recent incidents showed oscillation in embedding queue depth when multiple tenants burst simultaneously. Current autoscaler reacts to queue length with a fixed threshold which causes overshoot and long cold-start penalty for GPUs. This ticket designs and implements a hybrid approach: short-window rate smoothing + tenant-aware soft caps at the router, and a predictive autoscaler that uses short-term traffic forecasts and warmed idle pools to avoid cold starts. The change should be transparent to API consumers and respect existing per-tenant quotas and billing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 30-day benchmark: reduce p99 latency for embedding requests under burst scenarios by >=20% compared to baseline; 2) Reduce autoscaler overshoot events (scale-up followed by scale-down within 5 minutes) by >=50%; 3) Per-tenant rate smoothing must never drop below configured SLA priority buckets; 4) No increase in embedding request error rate >0.1% across test tenants; 5) Can toggle feature behind runtime flag and rollback to old scaler without data loss.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Router rate-smoothing (2 weeks): add a leaky-bucket style short-term rate window per-tenant (1s, 5s) and a soft-cap that marks requests for delayed enqueue if exceed smoothing window but under quota. Implement tagging so high-priority SLA tokens bypass or get larger windows. Phase 2: Predictive autoscaler (3 weeks): train a lightweight forecasting model (exponential smoothing / simple AR) using the last 60s of enqueue rate and sequence length distribution, expose a heuristic to pre-warm a small fraction of idle pools when forecast > threshold. Use a PID-style dampening factor to make scale decisions less binary. Phase 3: Integration and canary (1 week): implement rollout, telemetry, and circuit breaker to revert. Phase 4: Observability and cost analysis (1 week): add dashboards and alerting for overshoot, cold-start counts, and per-token unit cost. Rollout gated by acceptance criteria and stakeholder signoff.
rollout_plan: Default off. Canary to 5% of tenants for 48 hours using feature-flag targeting low-risk tenants. Monitor metrics; if unstable, increase smoothing window or rollback. After canary, expand to 25% for 72 hours, then 100% with weeks-long monitoring. Post-rollout: run a 7-day cost-lift analysis and verify no regressions in downstream reranking jobs.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Marco Ruiz: Kickoff meeting notes: product wants <25% latency regression for low-priority tenants. Ops raised concern over underutilized warm pools. Action: prototype short-window smoothing at router and mock autoscaler in staging.
2026-02-26 - Lena Patel: Engineering design doc shared: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Vector+Autoscaler+Heuristics. Key decision: use two smoothing windows (1s fast path, 10s dampening).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive pre-warming reduces p99 but increases operational cost; we decided to make pre-warm fraction tunable per-org and tie to committed capacity tiers. We considered fully machine-learning-based forecasting but chose lightweight exponential smoothing to reduce complexity and model drift. Router-level smoothing trades a small added enqueue delay for better batch utilization and fewer scale churn events.
